previous_versions: CAN 1.2 — Bosch CAN spec used through late 1980s; standard 11-bit identifier format only.
CAN 2.0 Part A — message format equivalent to CAN 1.2.
CAN 2.0 Part B — adds 29-bit extended identifier format; standard + extended messages coexist on same network.

key_changes.summary: Renamed/clarified CAN 1.2 11-bit identifier format; introduced four frame types (DATA / REMOTE / ERROR / OVERLOAD); fault confinement formalized.
Adds 29-bit extended identifier format; backward-compatible with Part A nodes provided extended-format messages are not used in mixed networks.
Upwards-compatible modifications increase max oscillator tolerance from 0.5 % to 1.5 % by allowing SOF at the 3rd INTERMISSION bit etc.

backward_compat_traps.Part_A_only_node: Sees the 29-bit extended identifier as a malformed standard frame.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Mixing Part-A and Part-B nodes is interoperable ONLY if no extended-format messages are used; introducing extended-format breaks Part-A nodes.

backward_compat_traps.spec_required: Transmitter sends r1 and r0 as dominant.
backward_compat_traps.receiver_required: Accept dominant AND recessive in all combinations (for forward compatibility with future protocol expansions).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Receivers that reject recessive r0/r1 break when interoperating with future Part C or CAN FD nodes.

backward_compat_traps.with_section_9_mods: Max oscillator tolerance 1.5 %; node treats dominant at 3rd INTERMISSION bit as new SOF.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Nodes without Section 9 modifications may interpret the 3rd-bit dominant as an OVERLOAD condition, generating a different bus behavior.

fields.version_naming_history_note: Bosch CAN 1.0 was internal (1986); CAN 1.2 was the widely deployed early-1990s automotive spec; CAN 2.0 (1991) introduced the Part A / Part B split. Later, ISO 11898 standardized CAN (1993) — ISO 11898-1 ≈ Bosch CAN 2.0 Part B, ISO 11898-2 specifies the high-speed physical layer, ISO 11898-3 the fault-tolerant low-speed PHY.
